newsitem.title: POLAND: BULK OF FOREIGN WITHDRAWAL FROM ZLOTY ENDED - FINMIN.
newsitem.headline: BULK OF FOREIGN WITHDRAWAL FROM ZLOTY ENDED - FINMIN.

text.p: The main wave of foreign investor withdrawal from zloty instruments, sparked last week by the fall of the Czech crown, is likely to have ended, Polish Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday.
"I think the main wave (of pulling out from zloty instruments) is over," Belka told a news conference.

Last Thursday and Friday the zloty dropped two percent against the basket of currencies as foreign investors sold the Polish unit to cut their central European exposure in general after the sharp fall of the Czech crown.

"I estimate that even if all the short-term, speculative capital left Poland, it would only have a minor effect on the zloty exchange rate," Belka said, adding he estimated the short-term cash parked in Poland totalled some $1.2 billion.

He also said the National Bank of Poland's small currency selling intervention last week to stop the zloty's fall proved very effective and made him confident the cental bank was in control of the situation.
Belka said that according to preliminary data the recent fast growth of credit for the economy slowed down in May, which bode well for curbing Poland's trade deficit.

The National Bank of Poland has been keeping high real interest rates since late last year to cool down domestic demand and therefore imports in order to keep Poland's fast growing trade gap under control.
